items.readable_text:
Content:
Given a fixed origin in the plane (often denoted [MATH: O]), and another point [MATH: X,] the vector [MATH: \overrightarrow{OX}] is called the position vector of the point [MATH: X.] The vector [MATH: \mathbf{x}] defines the position of [MATH: X] on the plane in relation to [MATH: O.]

Content:
For example, suppose we have two vectors [MATH: \overrightarrow{OA}=\mathbf{a}] and [MATH: \overrightarrow{OB}=\mathbf{b},] and a parallelogram [MATH: OAXB_1,] where [MATH: {OB_1}=2{OB}.] How can we find the vector [MATH: \mathbf{x},] the diagonal of the parallelogram, expressed in terms of [MATH: \mathbf{a}] and [MATH: \mathbf{b}?]

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/353e534f2f011d6ef99504860421ba2e]

Content:
From the [MATH: \triangle OB_1X] in the above figure, we can see that
[MATH: \mathbf{x} = \overrightarrow{OB}_1+\overrightarrow{B_1X}.]

Content:
We know that
[MATH: \overrightarrow{OB}_1=2\overrightarrow{OB}=2\mathbf{b}.]

Content:
Also, since [MATH: OAXB_1] is a parallelogram, we have [MATH: OA \parallel B_1X] and
[MATH: \overrightarrow{B_1X}=\overrightarrow{OA}=\mathbf{a}.]

Content:
Substituting these values into the original equality, we have

Content:
[MATH: x|= OB^(→)_{1} + B_{1}X^(→); = 2b + a; = a + 2b.]

sections.readable_text:
Consider the following diagram, where [MATH: \overrightarrow{OA}=\mathbf{a},] [MATH: \overrightarrow{OB}=\mathbf{b},] and [MATH: X] divides [MATH: AB] in the ratio [MATH: 3:1.] Find [MATH: \overrightarrow{OX}.]

[IMG: /graphics/8512f8ab1660315b7e5f0aa8beb302ff]

sections.normalized_html:
From the diagram, we see that [MATH: \overrightarrow{OX} = \overrightarrow{OA}+\overrightarrow{AX}.]

We're told that [MATH: \overrightarrow{OA} = \mathbf{a},] so we just need to work out [MATH: \overrightarrow{AX}.]

First, from [MATH: \triangle OAB,] we have

[MATH: AB^(→)|= AO^(→) + OB^(→); = − OA^(→) + OB^(→); = − a + b; = b − a.]

Since [MATH: AX:XB=3:1,] we have

[MATH: \overrightarrow{AX}=\dfrac{3}{4}\overrightarrow{AB}=\dfrac{3}{4}(\mathbf{b}-\mathbf{a}).]

Therefore,

[MATH: OX^(→)|= OA^(→) + AX^(→); = a + (3)/(4)(b − a); = (1)/(4)a + (3)/(4)b.]

lesson.readable_text:
Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
Given a fixed origin in the plane (often denoted [MATH: O]), and another point [MATH: X,] the vector [MATH: \overrightarrow{OX}] is called the position vector of the point [MATH: X.] The vector [MATH: \mathbf{x}] defines the position of [MATH: X] on the plane in relation to [MATH: O.]

Content:
For example, suppose we have two vectors [MATH: \overrightarrow{OA}=\mathbf{a}] and [MATH: \overrightarrow{OB}=\mathbf{b},] and a parallelogram [MATH: OAXB_1,] where [MATH: {OB_1}=2{OB}.] How can we find the vector [MATH: \mathbf{x},] the diagonal of the parallelogram, expressed in terms of [MATH: \mathbf{a}] and [MATH: \mathbf{b}?]

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/353e534f2f011d6ef99504860421ba2e]

Content:
From the [MATH: \triangle OB_1X] in the above figure, we can see that
[MATH: \mathbf{x} = \overrightarrow{OB}_1+\overrightarrow{B_1X}.]

Content:
We know that
[MATH: \overrightarrow{OB}_1=2\overrightarrow{OB}=2\mathbf{b}.]

Content:
Also, since [MATH: OAXB_1] is a parallelogram, we have [MATH: OA \parallel B_1X] and
[MATH: \overrightarrow{B_1X}=\overrightarrow{OA}=\mathbf{a}.]

Content:
Substituting these values into the original equality, we have

Content:
[MATH: x|= OB^(→)_{1} + B_{1}X^(→); = 2b + a; = a + 2b.]

---

[MATH: AB^(→)|= AO^(→) + OB^(→); = − OA^(→) + OB^(→); = − a + b; = b − a.]

Since [MATH: AX:XB=3:1,] we have

[MATH: \overrightarrow{AX}=\dfrac{3}{4}\overrightarrow{AB}=\dfrac{3}{4}(\mathbf{b}-\mathbf{a}).]

[MATH: OX^(→)|= OA^(→) + AX^(→); = a + (3)/(4)(b − a); = (1)/(4)a + (3)/(4)b.]
